{{Quote|The acquisition was a human named Jonmor Tinto. He'd been an accountant in a bank on Humbarine but was caught embezzling and sent to a Republic prison.|Cradossk, ''Making a Killing''|<ref name="Bounty Hunter Code" />}}
'''Humbarine''' was a [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] [[Ecumenopolis/Legends|city-planet]] and one of the [[Core Founder/Legends|founding members]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], having been originally [[Colonist/Legends|settled]] by [[Human/Legends|Humans]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kuat/Legends|Kuat]]. During the [[Tionese War]] of [[24,000 BBY]]&ndash;[[23,900 BBY]] Humbarine was the site of a Galactic Republic [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyard]]. A [[Bank/Legends|bank]] was located on the planet [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] prior to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], and the world was home to the military [[Officer/Legends|officer]] [[Barrow Oicunn/Legends|Barrow Oicunn]] and Republic [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Bana Breemu/Legends|Bana Breemu]] of the [[Humbarine sector/Legends|Humbarine sector]]. During the Clone Wars, Humbarine was repeatedly attacked by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], with Oicunn's family [[Death/Legends|perishing]] in the process. Ultimately, around [[20 BBY/Legends|20.2 BBY]] the [[Invisible Hand/Legends|flagship]] of Confederate [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] subjected the planet to an [[Bombardment of Humbarine/Legends|orbital bombardment]] that depopulated it and [[Temperature/Legends|melted]] its crust. Humbarine served the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] as a [[Fortress world/Legends|fortress world]] decades later.

==Description==
Humbarine was a [[Ecumenopolis/Legends|city-planet]]<ref name="Bombardment" /> located in the [[Humbarine system/Legends|Humbarine system]],<ref name="TEA" /> a part of the [[Humbarine sector/Legends|Humbarine sector]]<ref name="EAOC Humbarine" /> in the [[Arrowhead]], [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]] portion of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]. It was situated on the [[Trellen Trade Route/Legends|Trellen Trade Route]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]], which connected it to the [[Trellen system/Legends|Trellen system]] as well as the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies']] [[Commenor system/Legends|Commenor system]].<ref name="TEA" />

==History==
===An ancient colony===
[[File:Kuat_TEA.png|thumb|right|300px|Humbarine was settled by Humans from Kuat (pictured).]]
Humbarine was [[Colonist/Legends|settled]] by [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Sleeper ship/Legends|colonization arks]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kuat/Legends|Kuat]] of the nearby [[Kuat system/Legends|Kuat system]]. In turn, Humbarine eventually established colony worlds of its own, leading to the formation of the region known as the Humbarine Rule. At some point, however, the Colonies planets [[Balmorra/Legends|Balmorra]] and [[Commenor/Legends|Commenor]] declared their independence from Humbarine.<ref name="TEA" />

Once [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] technology was reverse-[[Engineer/Legends|engineered]] in the Core Worlds, Humbarine was among the planets that sent [[Merchant/Legends|traders]] and [[Scout/Legends|explorers]] out in [[Star map/Legends|uncharted]] [[Realspace/Legends|space]] in search of potential new worlds to claim. Humbarine, by that [[Time/Legends|time]] an emerging commerce hub, became one of the [[Core Founder/Legends|founding members]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]<ref name="TEA" /> upon that government's [[Galactic Constitution Conference|establishment]] in [[25,053 BBY]].<ref name="SWTOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

===Under the Republic===
{{Quote|Despite having served his sentence, ''[Jonmor Tinto]'' had an outstanding debt to a Humbarine industrialist who was not interested in reparations.|Cradossk, ''Making a Killing''|<ref name="Bounty Hunter Code" />}}
[[File:TheSpinCloseupAlsakanConflicts-EGTW.jpg|thumb|left|300px|During the conflicts between the Republic worlds Coruscant and Alsakan, Humbarine was allied with the former.]]
During the early stages of the [[Tionese War]],<ref name="EGTW" /> a [[Standard century/Legends|century]]-long conflict<ref name="TEA" /> fought between the Republic and the [[Honorable Union of Desevro and Tion|Honorable Union of Desevro & Tion]]<ref name="EGTW" /> beginning in [[24,000 BBY]],<ref name="TEA" /> Humbarine was the site of a Republic [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyard]]. After a [[Tionese (group)/Legends|Tionese]] invasion deep into the Core Worlds was repulsed, the [[Starship/Legends|starship]] manufacturing facility at Humbarine was among those that began the rapid construction of [[Warship/Legends|warships]], which the Republic used to further drive back the Tionese. Humbarine also remained loyal to the Republic [[Capital/Legends|capital]] world [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] during the early [[Alsakan Conflicts/Legends|Alsakan Conflicts]], a series of wars that [[First Alsakan Conflict|erupted]] around [[17,018 BBY]] and pitted the planet [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]] and its allies against those of Coruscant in a struggle for [[Politics/Legends|political]] control over the Republic.<ref name="EGTW" />

The ''[[Humbarine Housekeepers HoloBook]]'' was a [[Book/Legends|cookbook]]<ref name="NEGtD">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> published at some point several [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]] prior to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].<ref name="22 BBY">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]'' establishes that ''[[Humbarine Housekeepers HoloBook]]'' had been published several [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]] prior to the release of [[COO-series cook droid/Legends|COO cook droid]] model. That [[Cooking droid/Legends|droid]] model appeared in {{Film|II}}, the events of which ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].</ref> Humbarine was among the Core worlds that remained inside<ref name="TEA" /> the greatly diminished<ref name="EGTW" /> territory of the Republic during the [[Light and Darkness War|final phase]] of the [[New Sith Wars]] leading up to [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]].<ref name="TEA" /> Several [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Jonmor Tinto]] worked as an [[Accountant/Legends|accountant]] at a Humbarine [[Bank/Legends|bank]] before he was [[Prison/Legends|imprisoned]] by the Republic for embezzlement. Although Tinto was eventually released from prison, he subsequently became the target of [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] hired by a [[Unidentified Humbarine industrialist|Humbarine industrialist]], to whom Tinto was in debt. The hunter [[Cradossk/Legends|Cradossk]] ultimately captured Tinto on<ref name="Bounty Hunter Code" /> the [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]]<ref name="TEA" /> [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] and claimed the [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] on him. Cradossk later went on to mention Humbarine in his account of the capture of Tinto in his autobiography, ''[[Making a Killing]]''.<ref name="Bounty Hunter Code" />

===Clone Wars===
[[File:Senator_Bana_Breemu.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Republic Senator Bana Breemu of the Humbarine sector hailed from Humbarine.]]
During the Clone Wars, Humbarine remained within Republic borders,<ref name="TEA" /> and, during the first campaigns of the conflict in 22 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]], the Republic's [[Second Army|Second Sector Army]] was tasked with engaging the [[Confederacy military/Legends|military forces]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] in the planet's vicinity.<ref name="EGTW" /> [[Barrow Oicunn/Legends|Barrow Oicunn]], a junior [[Officer/Legends|officer]] with the Humbarine [[Sector/Legends|sector's]] [[Planetary Security Forces|defense forces]],<ref name="DB Oicunn">{{DB|character|ltoicunn|Oicunn, Lieutenant}}</ref> and [[Bana Breemu/Legends|Bana Breemu]], a [[Senator/Legends|senator]] who, during the Clone Wars, represented the sector in the Republic's [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]], both [[Homeworld/Legends|hailed]] from Humbarine.<ref name="DB Breemu">{{DB|character|banabreemu|Breemu, Bana}}</ref>

Eventually, some of the Humbarine sector's worlds joined the Confederacy,<ref name="CSWE HumbarineSector">{{CSWECite|II|67|Humbarine sector}}</ref> while others were infiltrated,<ref name="DB Breemu" /> conquered, or ravaged by the Confederate forces.<ref name="CSWE Breemu">{{CSWECite|I|93|Breemu, Bana}}</ref> Humbarine itself, left by the inefficiencies of the Republic [[Bureaucrat/Legends|bureaucracy]] with insufficient resources for its own protection, came under repeated devastating attacks led by [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], including a blitz that [[Death/Legends|killed]] Oicunn's family and as a result weakened the officer's faith in the Republic.<ref name="DB Oicunn" />

===Death of a world===
Grievous's [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], the [[Providence-class carrier/destroyer/Legends|''Providence''-class carrier/destroyer]] [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']],<ref name="DB TradeFederationCruiser">{{DB|starship|tradefederationcruiser|Trade Federation cruiser}}</ref> coordinated [[Confederate Navy/Legends|naval]] attacks on twenty-six Republic [[Loyalist/Legends|Loyalist]] worlds.<ref name="CSWE InvisibleHand" /> Around [[20 BBY/Legends|20.2 BBY]],<ref name="Bombardment" /> in an attack that horrified the inhabitants of the Core Worlds, on Grievous's orders,<ref name="TEA" /> the ''Invisible Hand'' subjected Humbarine to an [[Standard hour/Legends|hour]]-long [[Bombardment of Humbarine/Legends|orbital bombardment]] that depopulated the world and [[Temperature/Legends|melted]] its crust.<ref name="CSWE InvisibleHand" /> Balmorra eventually became home to many Humbariner [[Refugee/Legends|refugees]].<ref name="Author's Cut" />

During downtime on Coruscant, where Oicunn had been transferred as part of [[Coruscant Defense Fleet/Legends|Coruscant Home Fleet]], the [[Republic officer/Legends|officer]] met Breemu, with whom he had a sad conversation about Humbarine's desperate state. The senator, however, declared Oicunn a hero of Humbarine, bolstering his spirit and reinforcing his faith in the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] government.<ref name="DB Oicunn" /> After the [[Declaration of a New Order|formation]] of the Republic's successor, the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Humbarine was located within its territory,<ref name="EGTW" /> and between [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] and [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]], the planet served as an Imperial [[Fortress world/Legends|fortress world]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Inhabitants==
Originally settled by Humans from Kuat,<ref name="TEA" /> Humbarine served as the capital of the Humbarine sector.<ref name="CSWE Humbarine">{{CSWECite|II|66|Humbarine}}</ref> During the Clone Wars, the planet was depopulated.<ref name="CSWE InvisibleHand" /> Around [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], the population of the Humbarine [[Star system/Legends|system]] numbered between ten and one hundred million.<ref name="TEA" />

==Locations==
During the Tionese War, Humbarine hosted a Galactic Republic shipyard.<ref name="EGTW" /> Decades prior to the Clone Wars, the planet was the site of a bank.<ref name="Bounty Hunter Code" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Humbar is a back-formation from the planet Humbarine; I figured the planet was named after this family (maybe the original colonists?) but that was as much thought as I put into it.|Nathan O'Keefe|<ref name="TTSP endnotes">{{Blog|valinkenobi|14/comments|TTSP Endnotes: Volume 1}}</ref>}}
Humbarine was first mentioned in the reference book ''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith Incredible Cross-Sections]]'', authored by [[Curtis Saxton]]<ref name="RotSICS">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref> and published on [[April 2]], [[2005]].<ref name="Bookshelf">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iii/release/publishing/news20041124.html|text=Planning Your Episode III Bookshelf}}</ref> It was given its first visual depiction in an illustration by [[Ian Fullwood]] in<ref name="NEC" /> the [[October 25]], 2005<ref name="Random">{{RandomHouseOld|url=author/results.pperl?authorid=32326|text=Daniel Wallace}}</ref> reference book ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Kevin J. Anderson]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> and first appeared in the non-[[canon]]ical [[2009]] [[Star Wars video games|mobile game]] ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Mind Tricks]]''.<ref name="JMT">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Mind Tricks]]''</ref> Published on [[August 18]], 2009,<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> the reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed Humbarine in grid square M-10.<ref name="TEA" />

"[[Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji]]," an article authored by [[Nathan O'Keefe]] and published as part of the [[StarWars.com]] [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] feature on [[February 5]], 2009, mentions a legendary political dynasty named [[Humbar]].<ref name="Tinker">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/source/praji/20090205.html|text=Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji|int=Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji}}</ref> In his endnotes for the article, O'Keefe mentioned that "Humbar" was back-formed from the name of Humbarine and that the family may have been the planet's namesake and possibly its first settlers.<ref name="TTSP endnotes" />
